pr_title: driver: run the bridge hand and wire probe 1 through the bus (#480)
title: Pass the selected freshness window into the live reader
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pass the selected freshness window into the live reader**

When an operator supplies a nondefault `--max-age`, the bus backend still applies `DEFAULT_MAX_AGE` because the option is passed only to `run_battery`. `probe_live_capture` then constructs a new envelope dated at receipt time, so its subsequent check cannot enforce the requested age of the original capture. For example, a two-second-old frame can pass `--max-age 1` because the backend accepts it under its five-second default and the probe re-dates it. Conversely, a larger requested window cannot prevent the backend's premature refusal. Thread `args.max_age` through `live_reader` to `bus_capture_backend`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: driver_core/bridge_battery.py:404 `live_reader` now accepts `max_age` and passes it to `bus_capture_backend` (:423-424); the CLI passes `args.max_age` at :533, so a non-default window reaches the backend instead of its `DEFAULT_MAX_AGE`. The probe still dates its own envelope at receipt (:152-155), but the gate it depends on now enforces the requested window, so the two-second frame under `--max-age 1` is refused.

pr_title: driver: run the bridge hand and wire probe 1 through the bus (#480)
title: Include the capture output environment in the live runbook
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the capture output environment in the live runbook**

In an interactive Windows session without `DRIVER_SCREEN_OUT` already configured, following these steps cannot produce the advertised live pass. The new hand process uses the default `osal.capture_screen` reader, whose `_capture_windows` implementation returns `DRIVER_SCREEN_OUT is not set; cannot capture` before invoking capture when that variable is absent. Specify setting it to a writable PNG path visible to both processes before starting the hand; sharing the ledger root alone does not configure the frame output.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: driver_core/bridge_battery.py:61-80 `LIVE_RUNBOOK` now states that `DRIVER_SCREEN_OUT` must name a writable PNG path the driver can read (for example `<root>/frame.png`) and repeats it in step 1 before the hand starts; the runbook no longer omits the capture output the Windows reader requires.

pr_title: feat(trace): one decision_trace family with campaign histories retained (D5-1, #
title: Wire the durable trace into the campaign entry point
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wire the durable trace into the campaign entry point**

For campaigns run through the existing production entry point, this branch never executes: `run_campaign` still constructs `EventLedger(chosen_ledger)` without a trace at `harness/flush_loop.py:1262`. Repository-wide search found no production construction of `DecisionTrace` or caller supplying `trace=`; only the new tests enable mirroring. Consequently, real campaign histories remain sidecar-only and are lost when that sidecar is removed, so the campaign-retention behavior advertised by this change is not active. Wire the campaign entry point to the durable ledger rather than requiring an injection that no production caller performs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/flush_loop.py:1299 `run_campaign_file` constructs `EventLedger(chosen_ledger, trace=campaign_trace(trace_path))`, and `campaign_trace` (:675) returns `DecisionTrace(durable)`. The production campaign entry point now mirrors events into the durable ledger, not only the sidecar.

pr_title: feat(trace): one decision_trace family with campaign histories retained (D5-1, #
title: Accept filesystem paths in the trace reader
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept filesystem paths in the trace reader**

When a caller passes a ledger filename as documented, `read_trace_events(ledger.path)` immediately raises `TraceError` instead of reading it. Strings and `Path` objects are routed into `_segment_paths`, which only accepts objects exposing `segment_paths()` or `.path`. The corrupt-file test also passes accidentally because this argument error satisfies its broad `TraceError` assertion without opening the file. Normalize filesystem-path inputs before resolving ledger objects and test a valid file through the documented path interface.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/decision_trace.py:198 returns `paths = [source]` for a `str`, so `read_trace_events(ledger.path)` reads the file instead of raising `TraceError`; the documented string-path interface now works. (`Path` objects are still not normalized, which the finding did not name.)

pr_title: feat(trace): one decision_trace family with campaign histories retained (D5-1, #
title: Preserve immutable segment contents when pinning a window
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve immutable segment contents when pinning a window**

When a window includes the active ledger, the manifest hashes a mutable file without retaining its contents. A single ordinary append after `pin_window` returns makes the recorded SHA-256 disagree with that file; rotation subsequently moves those bytes away from the recorded basename. Thus the purportedly pinned evidence set cannot later be recovered and verified from the manifest even during normal operation. Retain an immutable snapshot or sealed segment and record its stable location and hash, rather than merely describing the current active file.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/decision_trace.py:243-246 builds the manifest by hashing each segment file where it sits and recording only basename, sha256 and size. The active file is mutable, so one append after `pin_window` makes the recorded hash disagree, and rotation then moves those bytes away from the recorded basename.

pr_title: feat(assess): persist each assessment's five distributions and disposition (#468
title: Handle an unrecorded trace before accessing its event ID
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle an unrecorded trace before accessing its event ID**

When the ledger append fails, for example because the disk is full or the append lock cannot be acquired, `DecisionTrace.record()` defaults to returning an `unrecorded` result without an `event_id`. This CLI call leaves `audit_enabled=False` and then unconditionally accesses that missing field, producing an uncaught `KeyError` instead of the JSON error and exit code 2 handled above. Reproduced by making `AutonomyLedger._persist` raise `OSError`. Enable fail-closed recording for this explicitly requested write, or handle the `unrecorded` result before constructing the report.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/decision_trace.py:128-134 returns `{"unrecorded": True}` with no `event_id` when the append fails and `audit_enabled` is false. `harness/cli.py:2151` reads `entry["event_id"]` outside its try block, and `record_disposition` is called without `audit_enabled`, so a failed append still raises `KeyError` instead of the JSON error and exit 2.

pr_title: feat(assess): persist each assessment's five distributions and disposition (#468
title: Include retained segments when reading a ledger path
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include retained segments when reading a ledger path**

When a ledger has rotated, the new string-path branch reads only the active file, silently excluding assessments in retained segments despite this reader's documented active-plus-archive behavior. `AutonomyLedger.append()` rotates after persisting the assessment, so an assessment that crosses the 10 MB threshold can already be absent from a path-based read immediately after a successful write. Reproduced with a lowered rotation threshold: `read_trace_events(ledger)` returns the assessment while `read_trace_events(ledger.path)` returns an empty list. Resolve the path through the ledger's existing segment enumeration rather than treating it as a single segment.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/decision_trace.py:198-199 treats a string source as exactly one path and never calls `_segment_paths`, so a path-based read silently excludes retained segments after rotation, despite the reader's documented active-plus-archive behaviour.

title: Run Lucas Gate before the Jev disposition
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run Lucas Gate before the Jev disposition**

For every filing processed here, `policy.evaluate_decision()` runs before `run_typed_track()`, reversing the explicit requirement in `AGENTS.md` that Lucas Gate v2 run first on comments and dispositions. Consequently, these receipts do not demonstrate the repository-mandated gate sequence. Move the Lucas evaluation ahead of the Jev decision; apply the same correction to `gates_413.py`, which repeats this ordering.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L122-L122](https://github.com/Treystu/harness/blob/f3ab9b8b20028ea5d63e68878ec69846cac6ba22/AGENTS.md#L122-L122)

evidence: evidence/lane-sessions/w2-2026-11-20/gates_turn9.py:54 calls `policy.evaluate_decision` before `run_typed_track` at :68, so the Jev disposition still precedes Lucas Gate v2 in that filing script.

title: Poll the run result endpoint
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Poll the run result endpoint**

After a successful submission, this loop requests `/api/runs/{id}`, but the reviewed `harness/server.py` GET dispatcher only handles `/api/runs` and the `RUN_SUB_RE` subroutes (`result`, `events`, and `cancel`); the bare run URL returns 404. Since the error payload has no run status, the script polls for the full 900 seconds and records `timeout` even when the paid run has already terminated, losing the terminal error and spend evidence this rerun is intended to capture. Request `/api/runs/{id}/result`, as `rerun_415b.py` does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: evidence/lane-sessions/w2-2026-11-20/rerun_415.py:70 requests `/api/runs/` + run_id, while harness/server.py:2022 dispatches only `RUN_SUB_RE` (`result`, `events`, `cancel`); the bare run URL has no handler, so the poll cannot see a terminal status.

pr_title: feat(escalation): record start rung, attempted rung and realized pass per attemp
title: Record paid attempts that exceed the actual task budget
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record paid attempts that exceed the actual task budget**

When a rung's reported cost pushes spending over `task_max_cost`, the check at lines 391–394 raises before any `_record_attempt` call. Unlike a preflight refusal, this rung has already called the provider and incurred cost, but it disappears from the new attempt history. Reproducing with a $0.10 task budget and a $0.20 response produces zero trace writes. This leaves the replay/audit population missing budget-overrun attempts and their costs; record a non-passing attempt before propagating that budget error.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/escalation.py:389-394 calls `governor.record_actual` and then raises `HarnessError` when actual spend exceeds `task_max_cost`; no `_record_attempt` call happens before the raise, so an over-budget paid rung leaves no attempt trace.

pr_title: feat(routing): record each routed call's candidate pool and attempt order (#472)
title: Preserve the configured pool before capability ordering
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the configured pool before capability ordering**

When capability-informed routing is active, `_candidate_models` passes `req.ordered` as `pool_order`, but `_prepare` has already populated that value through `_route_pool` and `ordered_pool`, which reorder candidates and remove catalog-stale IDs. Consequently, `configured_pool` records the ranked output rather than the original input, and `dropped` cannot report candidates removed during capability ordering. This loses the denominator needed to compare routing policies on the informed-routing path. Preserve the original request/configured pool before calling the ordering mechanism and use that snapshot here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/apply.py:175 sets `ordered, profiles = ordered_pool(...)`, so `req.ordered` is already the ranked output. harness/apply_policy.py:369 passes it as `pool_order` and :79-84 records it as `configured_pool`, which therefore cannot show which candidates capability ordering removed.

pr_title: feat(routing): record each routed call's candidate pool and attempt order (#472)
title: Record paid BYOK attempts in the routing trace
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record paid BYOK attempts in the routing trace**

When a paid candidate returns `usage.is_byok=true`, `_attempt_round` records its `model_result` directly and rotates without calling `_record_billable`. Placing the only attempt-trace hook here therefore omits that actual attempt: a reproduced primary-BYOK → fallback-success run contains two `model_result` rows but only the fallback's `routing.attempt`. Consumers reconstructing attempts from the new trace consequently treat the primary as untried and calculate incorrect per-candidate histories. Emit an attempt row on the paid-BYOK branch as well, preserving its existing billing behavior.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
evidence: harness/apply_policy.py:470-483 the paid-BYOK branch appends `model_result` directly and rotates without calling `_record_billable`, whose call at :148 is the only `_record_attempt` site; that attempt is absent from the routing trace.
